title: Products in the derived category are termwise
statement:
Let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and let $(K_i)_{i\in I}$ be a
family of complexes of $\mathcal R$-modules. Then the termwise product complex
$\prod_iK_i$ is a product of the $K_i$ in $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal R)$, and
$H^p(\prod_iK_i)\cong\prod_iH^p(K_i)$ for every $p$. If $K_i\to K'_i$ are
quasi-isomorphisms, so is $\prod_iK_i\to\prod_iK'_i$.

proof.text: Apply products_exact (det-pe-products-exact) to install exact limits of shape Discrete I in the given module universe. Apply isGrothendieckAbelianOfUniverses (lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck), with the independent site and coefficient universes, to obtain the Grothendieck instance. The existing K-injective resolution instance (lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective) then applies.

Use the already proved general PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete I) DerivedCategory.Q instance in WeilConjectures.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.TowerLimit and apply isLimitOfPreserves to limit.isLimit. Its proof is isLimitFanQ: choose K-injective resolutions, form their product in the homotopy category, use right orthogonality and the K-injective equivalence to obtain the derived product, and transport along the product quasi-isomorphism. Thus this implements the same K-injective route as the blueprint, for arbitrary I, and gives precisely Q.mapCone of the specified limit cone, including its projections.

The existing HomologicalComplex homologyFunctor preservation instance in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.DegreewiseLimits applies to exact limits of shape Discrete I. Consequently the standard piComparison for each p is an isomorphism. The general instance proves the cycles/images/cokernels calculation by applying the exact limit functor to short-complex homology; no derived-category products are assumed.

For the family f, form the discrete natural transformation with components f i. Install the component QuasiIso instances using the given hypothesis, and apply the already proved HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_limMap in WeilConjectures.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.TowerLimit. Its limit map is definitionally Limits.Pi.map f, so this is the third clause. The general lemma applies the exact limit functor to a complex in the diagram category and uses its preservation of homology.

lean.statement: theorem products_derived (X : Scheme.{t}) (R : Sheaf (topology X) RingCat.{max u (t + 1)}) (I : Type u) [HasDerivedCategory.{v} (ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R)] (K : I → CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R) ℤ) : Nonempty (IsLimit (DerivedCategory.Q.mapCone (limit.cone (Discrete.functor K)))) ∧ (∀ p : ℤ, IsIso (piComparison (HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor (ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) p) K)) ∧ (∀ (K' : I → CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R) ℤ) (f : ∀ i : I, K i ⟶ K' i), (∀ i : I, QuasiIso (f i)) → QuasiIso (Limits.Pi.map f))
